content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've been experiencing this issue for a long time and would appreciate any assistance. I have several [product_name] devices throughout the company, each with its own function, and they're all connected to the local network. I use my phone to log into them and gather process information. However, every time I access the IP address of a [product_name] device, I'm prompted with a login screen, even if no account has been configured. Is there something I might be doing incorrectly? Any help would be welcome! Thanks.
This behavior is standard. Whenever you leave the browser or change IP addresses in the browser window, the login screen will reappear each time you access the [product_name] device's IP.
I don't consider that to be 'normal', particularly since there is a "Keep me logged on" option available.
You may want to start a support request for this issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users repeatedly encounter login prompts when accessing the [product_name] web server, even after selecting the 'Keep me logged on' feature. Logging in is required each time the browser is closed or the device's IP address changes, which can disrupt workflow efficiency for those accessing multiple [product_name] devices. The existence of the 'Keep me logged on' option leads users to expect session persistence, but current behavior does not meet this expectation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that activating the 'Keep me logged on' feature will enable them to stay logged in across sessions, so they won't need to authenticate each time they access the [product_name] web server.
